title: 누가 까다롭게 굴어도 되는가 — 비친화성과 이중 잣대
summary: 두 진행자가 BBC Ideas의 말콤 글래드웰 영상 '세상은 왜 비친화적인 사람이 필요한가'를 영어로 깊이 파고들어요. 모두가 동의만 하는 사회는 유전자가 똑같은 단일 작물 밭처럼 취약하고, 마찰이 없으면 매끄러운 얼음 위처럼 앞으로 나아갈 수 없다는 것, 반대 의견을 막는 '나이트클럽 경비원' 관리자 대신 이상값을 반기는 '실험실 과학자'가 필요하다는 것, 그리고 같은 반항도 다수 집단 아이는 리더십으로, 소수 집단 아이는 불복종으로 읽히는 이중 잣대와 '성과의 특권'을 두 육상 선수 비유로 이야기해요.
topics: agreeableness · the Big Five · do not rock the boat
the monoculture crop · friction and traction on smooth ice
managers as nightclub bouncers vs. scientists in a lab
tolerating dissent vs. creating a safe place for it
the double standard · the luxury of being disagreeable · the two runners
구문: what if … · rather than · not A but B · only … if … · get to + 동사

grammar.title: ① 핵심 흐름 — 마찰은 왜 필요하고, 누가 마찰을 낼 수 있는가

head: 장면
핵심 문장
뜻
rows: Without variation or dissent, you have total vulnerability to changing circumstances.
If you want forward momentum, you need a surface with some bite.
Instead of a bouncer guarding the status quo, a manager needs to welcome strange new data.
현 상태를 지키는 경비원이 아니라 새 데이터를 반기는 사람
We want rebels, but only if they look a certain way.
You only get to privilege performance over behavior if you are in the group that is allowed to be disagreeable.
비친화적으로 굴어도 되는 집단만 행동보다 성과를 우선할 수 있다

grammar.tip: Being agreeable isn't always a personal choice. For millions of people, it is a forced survival mechanism.

grammar.title: ② What if …? — 만약 ~라면 어떨까요?
grammar.lead: 도입과 마무리에서 생각을 뒤집을 때 쓰는 질문이에요.
examples: What if that is the exact same trait that is holding human progress back?
그게 바로 인류의 진보를 막고 있는 특성이라면요?
Are we systematically locking away our greatest potential sources of innovation?
우리는 가장 큰 혁신의 원천을 체계적으로 가둬 두고 있는 걸까요? (마무리 질문)

grammar.title: ③ not A, but B / rather than / instead of
grammar.lead: 두 가지를 대비하는 표현이 계속 나와요.
examples: rewarding managers not for the silence and compliance of their teams, but for the actual quality of the debates they generate
팀의 침묵과 순종이 아니라 팀이 만드는 토론의 실제 질로 관리자를 보상하기
You are granted the grace to be judged by the results you produce, rather than how politely or quietly you produce them.
얼마나 공손하게 해냈느냐가 아니라 낸 결과로 평가받는 은혜를 받아요.
Instead of a bouncer guarding the status quo, a manager needs to be someone who actively welcomes strange new data.
현 상태를 지키는 경비원 대신, 관리자는 새 데이터를 반기는 사람이어야 해요.

grammar.title: ④ get to + 동사 — ~할 수 있게 되다, ~할 특권이 있다
grammar.lead: 허락이나 특권의 느낌이 있는 get to는 오늘 주제의 핵심 표현이에요.
examples: Who gets to push back on the boss, argue with the teacher, and be disagreeable without losing their standing?
누가 지위를 잃지 않고 상사에게 반박하고, 선생님과 논쟁하고, 비친화적으로 굴 수 있나요?
People on the inside get to be the brilliant, difficult, rule-breaking innovators.
안에 있는 사람은 똑똑하고 까다롭고 규칙을 깨는 혁신가가 될 수 있어요.
You only get to privilege performance over behavior if you are in the group that is allowed to behave in unusual ways.
특이하게 행동해도 되는 집단에 있을 때만 행동보다 성과를 우선할 수 있어요. (only … if …)

grammar.title: ⑤ 관용 표현 — rock the boat · thick skin · devil's advocate
grammar.lead: 직장과 학교 이야기에 자주 나오는 관용구예요.

head: 표현
뜻
예문
rows: The one who plays devil's advocate just to hear their own voice.
the ones with the thickest skins
You are grinning and bearing it.
They get the benefit of the doubt.

grammar.title: ⑥ 수동태로 말하는 낙인 — is perceived as / is labeled as / is reframed
grammar.lead: 같은 행동이 어떻게 '받아들여지는지'를 말할 때 수동태를 써요.
examples: It is immediately perceived as a threat.
곧바로 위협으로 받아들여져요.
It is labeled as insubordination, defiance, or just a strict disciplinary issue.
불복종, 반항, 아니면 엄한 징계 문제로 낙인찍혀요.
It is often reframed, isn't it?
종종 다르게 포장되잖아요?

grammar.title: ⑦ 비유로 설명하기 — Imagine … / Think about … / It's like …
grammar.lead: 진행자들은 추상적인 생각을 그림으로 바꿔요. 따라 하면 설명 실력이 늘어요.
examples: Think about a massive field where every single plant is genetically identical.
모든 식물이 유전적으로 똑같은 거대한 밭을 생각해 보세요.
Like trying to walk across a frozen lake in smooth-soled shoes.
바닥이 매끈한 신발로 얼어붙은 호수를 건너려는 것처럼요.
Imagine putting two runners on a track for a really high-stakes race.
아주 중요한 경주를 위해 트랙에 선수 두 명을 세운다고 상상해 보세요.

phrases: But I have to push back on this a little bit.
That exhaustion is kind of the price of admission for progress.
그 피로가 진보의 입장료 같은 거예요.
Attacking the person versus the idea.
We want rebels, but only if they look a certain way.
반항아를 원하긴 하는데, 특정한 모습일 때만이죠.
They simply cannot afford the luxury of being disagreeable.
비친화적으로 구는 사치를 누릴 형편이 안 돼요.
It really does change the lens on everything.
정말 모든 걸 보는 렌즈를 바꿔 놓네요.

quiz.q: According to the hosts, what does society usually reward?
options: Playing nice and not rocking the boat
quiz.explain: Society rewards you for playing nice, but history only really remembers the people who didn't.

quiz.q: Which source is this deep dive based on?
options: A TED talk by Adam Grant
A BBC Ideas video featuring Malcolm Gladwell
quiz.explain: We have this transcript from BBC Ideas featuring Malcolm Gladwell, titled "Why the World Needs Disagreeable People."

quiz.q: Why is an entirely agreeable society compared to a monoculture crop?
options: It looks perfect but is fragile because it lacks variation
quiz.explain: Because there is zero genetic friction, zero variation, it is incredibly fragile.

quiz.q: What does the frozen lake example show?
options: Without friction, you cannot move forward
quiz.explain: On perfectly smooth ice there is zero friction, and you cannot move forward. You need resistance.

quiz.q: Many managers measure their success by …
options: a lack of friction — a quiet team that never argues
quiz.explain: They genuinely believe that a lack of friction is how their success ought to be measured.

quiz.q: Who does Gladwell say ought to be in management positions?
options: The people with the thickest skins
quiz.explain: The people who ought to be in management positions are the ones with the thickest skins.

quiz.q: What is the difference between productive friction and toxic behavior?
options: Productive friction challenges ideas; toxic behavior attacks individuals
quiz.explain: Productive friction is about challenging ideas, processes and assumptions. Toxic behavior is about attacking individuals.

quiz.q: A good manager should be like …
options: a scientist thrilled to discover an anomaly in the data
a referee who stops every argument
quiz.explain: You transition from being a bouncer to being a scientist… because the anomaly is where the new discovery hides.

quiz.q: According to Gladwell, society's tolerance of disruptive behavior is conditional on …
quiz.explain: Conditional based on identity and power.

quiz.q: In the two-runner analogy, what does the first runner (the disadvantaged child) focus on?
options: Perfect, polite form so as not to be disqualified
quiz.explain: Their entire mental capacity is focused on not breaking a single rule, just to avoid being disqualified.

quiz.q: "Who ___ push back on the boss without losing their job?" (특권의 느낌)
quiz.explain: get to + 동사 = ~할 수 있게 되다, ~할 특권이 있다.

quiz.q: What challenge do the hosts leave you with?
options: Look around at who is allowed to be difficult and who is punished for it
quiz.explain: Look closely at who is actually allowed to be difficult… and who is immediately punished.
